title: Lifting a bounded above acyclic complex of modules of the form P over IP to an acyclic complex whose terms lie in a class stable under summands and surjectivity modulo the ideal
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The statement fixes a ring R, an ideal I, a class of R-modules closed under direct summands and stable under maps that are surjective modulo I, and asks that every bounded above acyclic complex whose terms are of the form P over IP with P in the class be lifted to a bounded above acyclic complex with terms in the class (statement lines 19342-19357). The proof is a downward induction on the degree under a vanishing bound: at each step the already lifted part is split as P^i = Z^i direct sum Z^{i+1} so that closure under summands keeps the cycles inside the class, and the next term is built from the projectivity of P^{n-1} together with the identification Z^n/IZ^n = Im(E^{n-1} -> E^n), after which property (3) upgrades the lifted map to a surjection (proof lines 19373-19383). What is not routine is maintaining three properties at once through the induction, namely the isomorphism modulo I, acyclicity in all degrees above the running index, and membership of every cycle in the class, which is why the two closure hypotheses are needed in exactly this form. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing.
